question: A 5-year-old boy has accidentally ingested peanuts. In which bronchus will you find it lodged most likely?
explanation: The right main bronchus is wider, shorter, and more vertical than the left main bronchus. When a foreign body is aspirated, it is much more likely to fall into the right main bronchus. While the inferior lobe bronchus is a common lodging site within the right lung.

question: An infant presents with severe respiratory distress, and examination reveals decreased breath sounds on the left side of the chest. Imaging confirms that Loop of intestines are present within the left thoracic cavity. This congenital defect is caused by the failure of which membrane to properly fuse during fetal development?

options.D: Failure of the muscular ingrowth from the body wall

explanation: This describes a Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia typically a Bochdalek hernia. This condition results from the failure of the posterior-lateral part of the diaphragm—derived from the pleuroperitoneal membranes—to fuse completely with the other parts of the diaphragm, allowing abdominal viscera to enter the chest cavity.
